Updated assessment incorporating the April 2023 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS):
- The FOMC statement (May 3, 2023) notes modest growth, robust employment, elevated inflation, and highlights that tighter credit conditions are likely to weigh on activity, hiring, and inflation; policy was tightened to 5–5.25% with ongoing balance-sheet runoff.
- The April 2023 SLOOS corroborates and amplifies the downside risks: banks broadly tightened lending standards and terms across C&I and commercial real estate (wider spreads, lower loan-to-value ratios, higher debt-service coverage), citing a weaker economic outlook, higher funding costs, deposit outflows, and liquidity concerns. Demand for C&I loans weakened (notably for plant/equipment, M&A, inventory, and A/R financing). Consumer credit saw tighter standards/terms across autos, HELOCs, residential mortgages (QM and non-QM), and other consumer loans; credit card demand was roughly unchanged, but terms tightened. Banks and foreign banks expect further tightening ahead.
- These SLOOS findings suggest a more pronounced prospective drag on credit availability and real activity than the FOMC statement alone, reinforcing vulnerabilities (especially CRE) and elevating downside risk to growth and hiring despite still-strong labor data.

Net effect: more negative than the initial read and the FSR-adjusted view; sentiment nudged further down.
